sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Library list with minimum versions
sections.what: Lists the libraries for AI, document reading, data handling, charts, notebooks, the web page and utilities. Users see nothing directly; setup.sh installs the list.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps every dependency in one place so a new computer can be set up with one command.
sections.watch_out: Minimum versions only, so a future release can break the app, and several packages such as jupyter and seaborn are not imported by any visible file.

summary: The list of Python libraries the project needs, each with a minimum version.
purpose: Tells pip, Python's package installer, which libraries to install.
why: Likely reason: one list lets setup.sh install everything in a single command. The first comment states Python 3.10 or newer is required.
how: pip reads each line, installs the named package at the stated minimum version or newer, and installs the packages those depend on.
outputs: Installed packages in the venv folder created by setup.sh.
risks: Minimum versions allow future releases that may break the app. Several packages (jupyter, ipywidgets, seaborn, kaleido, matplotlib, tqdm, tenacity) do not appear in the visible files, so their use is unclear.
debug: If installation fails, read the first error line from pip; version conflicts usually name the two packages involved. Re-run setup.sh after editing this file.
